mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate environment reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing the present value of future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% signals aggressive monetary easing, which typically precedes positive equity market performance as investors anticipate improved economic conditions over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS falls below 2.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling does not produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: High housing market activity (HOUST > 1000) reflects strong consumer confidence and demand for goods, which typically supports positive equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 1000, the S&P 500 delivers negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing output and economic activity, which correlates with positive equity market returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits expand.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment rates (UNRATE > 6.0) signal economic distress and reduced consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 6.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stable or rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) indicate monetary tightening, which suppresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5pp in 3 months AND FEDFUNDS > 3.0%
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL rising >0.5pp and FEDFUNDS >3.0% does not result in negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle, signaled by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0%, increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, the S&P 500 delivers positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances.
